original_question: Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of m-orbit polytopes.
target_in_paper: The open problem in the paper’s realizations section asking for a realization theory that relates faithful geometric k-orbit realizations to underlying abstract m-orbit polytopes.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies that the target is a realizations problem, and it preserves the paper’s core theme of comparing the flag-orbit count of an abstract polytope with the flag-orbit count of a geometric realization.
missing_details: The draft does not define an abstract m-orbit polytope: namely, an abstract polytope whose automorphism group has exactly m orbits on flags.
It does not define a realization in a geometric space S, starting from a map on vertices and the induced images of higher-rank faces.
It does not say whether the realization is required to be faithful; this matters because orbit-count comparisons are most naturally stated for faithful realizations.
It does not say whether the realization is required to be symmetric, i.e. whether automorphisms of the abstract polytope are represented by geometric symmetries of the realization.
It does not define a k-orbit realization: namely, that the geometric symmetry group of the realized geometric polytope has exactly k orbits on flags.

It leaves implicit the relation between the abstract automorphism group and the geometric symmetry group; in the faithful symmetric setting, the latter is naturally a subgroup of the former, so the geometric orbit count refines the abstract one.
It does not specify the intended scope of the theory: the paper’s intent is a realization theory for k-orbit phenomena, not a broad classification problem far beyond that context.
It does not indicate whether the problem is meant for finite and infinite polytopes, or for realizations in an arbitrary geometric space S rather than a fixed Euclidean dimension.
It does not unpack the paper-faithful meaning of the phrase 'k-orbit realizations of m-orbit polytopes' into a stand-alone mathematical question.
refined_question: Develop a realization theory for abstract m-orbit polytopes: given an abstract polytope K whose automorphism group has exactly m flag-orbits, determine and describe the faithful symmetric geometric realizations of K in a geometric space S whose geometric symmetry group has exactly k flag-orbits; equivalently, make precise for which integers k such k-orbit realizations of an abstract m-orbit polytope can occur, and how they should be studied in a systematic realization-theoretic framework.
justification: The paper is an open-problems survey on k-orbit abstract polytopes, and your draft clearly points to its realizations part rather than to a broader construction or symmetry-type-graph problem. The nearest paper-faithful target is the realizations-section problem about building a theory for k-orbit realizations of abstract m-orbit polytopes. To make that question stand alone, one must unpack the two orbit counts: m for the abstract automorphism action on flags, and k for the geometric symmetry action on flags of a realization. The refined version keeps the paper’s intent narrow by staying in realization theory and by making explicit the standard hidden assumptions from this context—abstract polytope K, geometric space S, faithful realization, symmetry-induced action, and flag-orbit counts—without broadening the problem into unrelated classification programs. The instruction to prioritize Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3 does not apply here, because this paper is an open-problems survey organized by topic rather than by an initial conjecture-theorem sequence; the relevant target is the realizations section near the end of the paper.
